On September 24, 1988, Johnson won the 100m final at the Summer Olympics in Seoul, lowering his own world record to 9.79 seconds. Johnson would have been even faster had he not coasted to the line and raised his hand in the air. However, the Olympic Doping Control Center found that Johnson's blood and urine samples contained stanozolol, and he was disqualified three days later.

American Carl Lewis was given the gold medal even though race footage shows that he ran out of his lane two or three times, which should have resulted in automatic disqualification. Later, six of the eight finalists tested positive for banned drugs or were implicated in a drug scandal at some point in their careers.

Johnson's coach Charlie Francis admitted that his athletes were taking anabolic steroids, as he claims all top athletes at the time were, and also said that Johnson could not possibly have tested positive for stanozolol since he preferred furazabol. André Jackson, Carl Lewis' Santa Monica Track Club teammate, who was inside the drug testing room in Seoul, infers in the 30 for 30 documentary and is alleged to have admitted to having placed the stanozolol in one of the bottles Johnson drank from in order to make urine for his test.
